articles.body:
IonQ (IONQ) just inked a multi-year alliance with South Korea based SDT Inc., focused on delivering its Superion 256 quantum computer and SiV memory, and on building a dedicated quantum manufacturing hub in Gumi.

Set against a 1-day share price return of 0.57% and a 7-day share price gain of 9.96%, IonQ's recent SDT deal and Superion 256 launch come after a tougher stretch where the 90-day share price return fell 23.99% and the 1-year total shareholder return declined 45.78%, even though the 3-year total shareholder return remains very large at about 3x, signalling strong long term momentum but a more cautious recent reset around execution and risk.

Scan beyond IonQ and see how other quantum and AI infrastructure plays stack up in our hand picked list of 25 quantum computing stocks .

IonQ now trades at a steep 65% discount to the average analyst target even after the SDT news bounce. Is that caution around losses and execution discipline, or has sentiment swung too far?

IonQ's most followed valuation story pegs fair value around $48 per share, which sits above the last close at $40.74 and presents the stock as discounted relative to that narrative anchor.

IonQ's biggest advantage is still the same one it had before, but it is more visible now, it is the best-funded, broadest, and most commercially scaled public quantum company. At the end of 2025, IonQ had $3.3 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and investments, which remains an enormous strategic asset in a capital-intensive sector.

According to HedgeY, this combination of a large cash reserve, a broad quantum platform, and commercial traction supports a fair value of $48 per share, which implies IonQ trades at roughly a 15% discount to that narrative estimate today. The same narrative highlights valuation, execution risk, and continued losses as important counterweights, so that $48 is presented as a balanced view rather than a one-sided bullish call.

Still, IonQ's heavy losses of US$1.36b on just US$246.47m of revenue, along with the recent 1 year share price decline of 45.78%, could quickly pressure that 15% undervalued story.

IonQ can appear inexpensive from one perspective and costly from another. On a price-to-book ratio of 4.9x, the stock trades slightly above the US Semiconductor industry at 4.6x but well below its peer group at 12x. That combination suggests both downside risk and upside potential. Which crowd is right?

articles.title: Anac atualiza regras sobre atrasos e cancelamentos de voos; entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresas ficam isentas de responsabilidade civil em casos de força maior, como eventos climáticos, mas seguem obrigadas a prestar assistência.
articles.summary: Regras da Anac para voos agora isentam aéreas de indenizar por mau tempo, mas mantêm a obrigatoriedade de auxílio com alimentação e hospedagem aos passageiros.
articles.body:
A Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac) aprovou nesta terça-feira (22) uma atualização das regras que tratam dos direitos dos passageiros em casos de atraso e cancelamento de voos.

Segundo a agência, as mudanças têm como objetivo ampliar a transparência das informações prestadas aos clientes para facilitar a compreensão sobre seus direitos, o funcionamento do transporte aéreo e as obrigações das companhias aéreas diante de imprevistos.

Em situações decorrentes de caso fortuito ou força maior, como eventos climáticos, as empresas ficam isentas de responsabilidade civil pelos impactos causados.

Segundo o Código Brasileiro de Aeronáutica (CBA), se enquadram ocorrências como restrições ao pouso ou à decolagem decorrentes de condições meteorológicas adversas impostas por órgão do sistema de controle do espaço aéreo; restrições ao pouso ou à decolagem decorrentes de indisponibilidade da infraestrutura aeroportuária; dentre outros.

Por outro lado, permanece obrigatório a assistência material, nos seguintes casos:

🕒Após duas horas: alimentação, por meio de crédito, refeição ou solução equivalente;

🕒Após quatro horas, quando houver necessidade de pernoite : hospedagem e transporte de ida e volta ao local de acomodação.

A nova regra também esclarece que a prestação de assistência não se confunde com reconhecimento da culpa ou dever de responsabilização

As novas regras passam a valer 30 dias após a publicação no Diário Oficial da União (DOU), período destinado à adaptação das empresas aéreas às novas regras.

Outra mudança prevê que as companhias aéreas poderão reembolsar gastos com alimentação, transporte e hospedagem quando situações excepcionais.

Entre elas estão: limitações da infraestrutura aeroportuária, falta comprovada de fornecedores locais ou emergências imprevisíveis, impedirem o fornecimento direto da assistência.

Nesses casos, o passageiro deverá comprovar as despesas necessárias e razoáveis que realizou com alimentação, transporte ou hospedagem. O reembolso deverá ser feito em até sete dias.

A Anac definiu ainda que o passageiro, quando estiver adquirindo a passagem, deve ser informado de que a operação aérea pode sofrer alterações devido a condições meteorológicas, requisitos de segurança e outros fatores que podem alterar a execução do voo.

A medida, segundo a Anac, visa dar mais transparência ao passageiro.

Também foi estabelecido que, tão logo tenha conhecimento de atraso, cancelamento ou interrupção do serviço, a empresa deverá comunicar o passageiro por canais digitais e manter as informações atualizadas.

A comunicação deverá indicar a previsão de partida, as alternativas de reacomodação disponíveis e a forma de acesso à assistência material, como alimentação e hospedagem.

articles.title: Comissão da ONU alerta: Super El Niño pode tirar 2% do PIB | G1
articles.standfirst: Fenômeno climático pode afetar agricultura, geração de energia e pesca; estimativa considera um cenário de El Niño extremo na região
articles.summary: Fenômeno climático pode afetar agricultura, geração de energia e pesca; estimativa considera um cenário de El Niño extremo na região
articles.body:
Um episódio extremo do El Niño pode reduzir em pelo menos 2% o Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) da América Latina e do Caribe ao longo de três anos e levar até 4,8 milhões de pessoas adicionais à pobreza até o fim da década, segundo estimativa da Comissão Econômica para a América Latina e o Caribe (Cepal), órgão ligado à Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU).

A estimativa consta de um relatório especial divulgado nesta segunda-feira (21). O estudo analisa os possíveis impactos econômicos, sociais e ambientais de um episódio de El Niño de forte intensidade na região.

Segundo a Cepal, cerca de metade da perda econômica estimada ocorreria já no primeiro ano do fenômeno. A redução da renda das famílias também poderia ampliar o número de pessoas em situação de pobreza em relação a um cenário sem El Niño.

O El Niño é um fenômeno climático caracterizado pelo aquecimento anormal das águas do Oceano Pacífico Equatorial. Essa mudança altera a circulação da atmosfera e pode modificar o regime de chuvas e temperaturas em diferentes partes do mundo.

A intensidade do fenômeno pode variar. No cenário analisado pela Cepal, um episódio extremo teria efeitos mais severos sobre a economia e sobre setores como agricultura, energia e pesca.

Sim. Segundo o relatório da Cepal, projeções da Administração Nacional Oceânica e Atmosférica dos Estados Unidos (NOAA) apontam mais de 90% de probabilidade de o El Niño atingir intensidade muito forte durante o outono e o inverno do Hemisfério Norte de 2026-2027 (primavera e verão no Brasil).

A NOAA também estima 69% de probabilidade de o fenômeno atingir uma magnitude histórica, classificada no relatório como "Súper El Niño". Nesse cenário, a temperatura da superfície do mar na região conhecida como Niño 3.4 apresentaria anomalias superiores a 2,5°C ou 3°C.

Isso não significa, porém, que a perda de 2% do PIB ou o aumento da pobreza necessariamente ocorrerão. Esses números são estimativas da Cepal para um cenário de El Niño extremo.

Os efeitos não seriam distribuídos igualmente entre os países ou setores da economia. A Cepal prevê impactos sobre o PIB, inflação, pobreza e produção e destaca riscos especialmente para energia, agricultura, pesca e infraestrutura.

Um dos principais pontos de atenção é o setor elétrico. Segundo o relatório, vários países da América Latina dependem fortemente da geração hidrelétrica: em alguns deles, as hidrelétricas respondem por mais de 70% da matriz elétrica.

Com menos chuva e temperaturas mais altas, os reservatórios podem ficar sob pressão justamente quando aumenta a demanda por eletricidade para refrigeração e ar-condicionado.

A Cepal estima que, entre outubro e dezembro de 2026, a probabilidade de déficit de precipitação chega a 60% em determinadas áreas, enquanto 31,1% do território regional estaria em alerta alto. Grandes cidades, como São Paulo, Lima e Cidade do México, poderiam enfrentar aumento da demanda por energia em períodos de menor disponibilidade hídrica.

A agricultura também está entre os setores mais vulneráveis.

➡️ Com base em análises da Organização das Nações Unidas para a Alimentação e a Agricultura (FAO), a Cepal aponta probabilidade superior a 70% de ocorrência de secas que afetem a atividade agropecuária nos próximos meses em áreas do Corredor Seco da América Central, além de regiões da Colômbia, Venezuela e países do Caribe, como Cuba, República Dominicana e Haiti.

O risco envolve redução das colheitas, menor disponibilidade de alimentos e de forragem para os animais e perda de renda para produtores rurais.

O El Niño também altera as condições do Oceano Pacífico e pode prejudicar a atividade pesqueira.

O aquecimento das águas enfraquece a subida de águas profundas e frias, um processo que leva nutrientes para a superfície e sustenta parte da cadeia alimentar marinha. Com menos nutrientes disponíveis, espécies como anchoveta, sardinha e merluza podem migrar ou ter sua disponibilidade reduzida.

A Cepal cita episódios anteriores de intensidade excepcional nos quais as capturas pesqueiras da região caíram 52,7% em 1972-1973 e 26,9% em 1997-1998.

Por que o fenômeno pode aumentar a pobreza?

O impacto econômico do El Niño não fica restrito ao clima.

Uma quebra de safra, por exemplo, pode reduzir a renda de produtores e trabalhadores rurais e, ao mesmo tempo, pressionar os preços dos alimentos. Problemas na geração de energia podem elevar custos para empresas e consumidores. Já perdas na pesca afetam comunidades que dependem diretamente da atividade.

É a combinação desses efeitos que pode atingir a renda das famílias e aumentar o número de pessoas abaixo da linha de pobreza.

No cenário extremo analisado pela Cepal, até 4,8 milhões de pessoas adicionais poderiam entrar na pobreza até o fim da década em relação a um cenário sem El Niño.

A Cepal recomenda medidas para tentar reduzir os impactos antes que eles ocorram. Entre elas estão a criação de mecanismos financeiros para situações de emergência, investimentos em infraestrutura mais resistente a eventos climáticos, sistemas de alerta, proteção de famílias vulneráveis e medidas para reduzir a dependência de uma única fonte de geração de energia.

O órgão também recomenda o planejamento de estoques e recursos para períodos de seca, maior integração energética entre países e medidas para aumentar a eficiência no consumo de eletricidade.

A avaliação da Cepal é que medidas preventivas tendem a custar menos do que respostas adotadas apenas depois de uma emergência.

articles.title: President Trump’s money managers made more than 1,100 trades in July
articles.summary: President Donald Trump’s money managers made 1,152 trades on his behalf in July alone, according to his latest financial disclosure Tuesday — an astronomical...
articles.body:
President Donald Trump's money managers made 1,152 trades on his behalf in July alone, according to his latest financial disclosure Tuesday — an astronomical number relative to his predecessors, and still high by the standard of active traders.

The transactions included many companies such as SpaceX and RTX (formerly known as Raytheon) that do business with the federal government, in industries his administration helps regulate.

The financial transactions amount to roughly 50 trades a day, a heavy volume for a typical investor but consistent with Trump's portfolio activity in his second term. According to a Bloomberg analysis , Trump or his managers have executed more than 28,000 trades since his second inauguration in January 2025 — more than every member of the House and Senate, combined.

Former presidents Joe Biden and Barack Obama didn't trade individual stocks, as their portfolios relied primarily on mutual funds and US Treasuries.

The scale of the trading — which included as much as $25 million in sales of shares of both Microsoft and Amazon — has deepened concerns about the potential for corruption.

The amount of turnover "does seem high," even by the standards of a tactical investor trying to time the market, said Brett Bernstein, CEO and co-founder of XML Financial Group. But even if the "optics aren't always great," the volume alone doesn't necessarily indicate corruption.

"It depends on someone's approach to investing… if they have a tactical portfolio manager that's timing markets with strategies, it doesn't seem overly crazy," Bernstein added.

Trump declined to place his assets in a blind trust – meaning he has the ability to see which stocks his money managers are buying or selling. Trump's signature appears on his financial disclosure form listing all of his trades, indicating he has seen the document and is aware of at least some of his holdings.

"President Trump's stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third-party financial institutions," Davis Ingle, a White House spokesperson, told CNN.

"All holdings are maintained in discretionary accounts and invested through computer-based model portfolios that automatically replicate recognized indexes, such as the Schwab 1000. Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence, or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold. All investment decisions are made entirely by independent managers. There are no conflicts of interest," Ingle added.

articles.title: No rule stops airport cos from having airlines: Govt
articles.summary: India Business News: NEW DELHI: Govt is weighing the pros and cons of allowing airport operators such as Adani Group, which operates Mumbai Airport, to run an airline, alt.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Govt is weighing the pros and cons of allowing airport operators such as Adani Group, which operates Mumbai Airport, to run an airline, although no decision has been taken yet. The Delhi and Mumbai airports went the PPP way in 2006 and their “operation, management and development agreement” (OMDA) does not allow the operators to have beyond 10% stake in an airline. Recently, the Adani Group had sought an amendment to the same.“Govt is clear that India needs more airlines, given the number of airports going to come up in India and the demand. Our ambition is to have at least five airlines with at least 100 aircraft each. So, if someone wants to start an airline, govt supports the idea. The issue is an airport (Mumbai and Delhi) doing so. We are examining the pros and cons of the same,” civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said here Tuesday.Naidu said no decision on the Adani request has been taken so far. “We need to create a system where the cons (of allowing such a move) are taken care of. Pros we know. As such in govt there is no clause or rule anywhere which stops airport operators from having airlines other than the OMDA agreement for Delhi and Mumbai. If BIAL (Bengaluru operator), which is a private operator, wants to operate an airline, there is no rule stopping him. That’s why we have to take a balanced approach,” said Naidu.Adani’s request has divided the airline industry with IndiGo promoter Rahul Bhatia opposing the move and Akasa founder Vinay Dube being in favour of the same.The minister spoke about other issues at an UDAN event. “Aviation ministry, Airports Authority of India and 21 States and UTs (have) come together and sign MoUs to put a greater focus on speed, sustainability and long-term viability of projects in the next phase of UDAN… 100 airports will be developed under challenge mode over the next 10 years,” Naidu said.SpiceJetThe cash-strapped airline’s woes have been mounting and its passengers often suffer delays running in several hours. “We are closely monitoring SpiceJet’s operations and finances through the aviation regulatory body to ensure safety is not compromised,” Naidu said.Dope test on pilots“The intention of the ministry is that all pilots must get tested within a year. The framework for the same has to be issued by the regulator DGCA,” said the minister.No fare caps this festive seasonAirfares will not be capped this festive season and the aviation ministry will advise airlines to keep the same at reasonable levels, said Naidu. The recent hike being seen is not due to spike in demand but due to increased jet fuel prices. “We definitely make a point to them (airlines) that during this festive season, you have to ensure that fair prices are kept at a reasonable level so that people who want to travel, get to see the benefit,” the minister said.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Wall Street’s Nasdaq hits all-time high as AI frenzy gathers pace
articles.summary: Investors shrug off AI safety concerns and Iran war, sending market to a new peak.
articles.body:
Wall Street’s Nasdaq stock exchange has hit an all-time high, shrugging off concerns about AI safety risks, sky-high tech valuations and the energy shock caused by the United States’ war on Iran.

The Nasdaq Composite index, which is dominated by US tech giants such as Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft, rose 0.45 percent on Tuesday, taking its gains to date this year to more than 17 percent.

The Nasdaq 100, a narrower index that tracks 100 top companies, jumped 0.82 percent.

The S&P 500, the most popular measure of the overall US stock market, closed essentially flat.

Monolithic Power Systems, a Florida-based manufacturer of power circuits, and Canadian e-commerce company Shopify led the gains, surging 8.1 percent and 7.1 percent, respectively.

Micron Technology, one of the world’s top three memory chip makers along with South Korea’s SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, rose 5 percent.

Chip giant Nvidia, the world’s most valuable company, gained 0.7 percent, while Apple edged up 0.2 percent.

Meta Platforms, which soared 11.4 percent on Monday on excitement surrounding its new AI assistant Muse, dropped 0.63 percent.

Major Asian stock markets opened higher on Wednesday, with Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 and South Korea’s Kospi up about 1.4 percent and 0.1 percent, respectively, in morning trading.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index opened lower, falling more than 0.7 percent during the morning trade.

Oil prices were largely flat on Tuesday, after falling more than 3 percent the previous day amid improving oil flows out of the Gulf and hopes of renewed diplomacy between Washington and Tehran.

Futures for Brent crude, the international benchmark, were trading at $99.18 a barrel as of 01:00 GMT.

⁠US President Donald Trump on Tuesday told reporters that US officials ‌held a “very good” meeting with their Iranian counterparts on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, hours after using his address to the session to warn that he could “annihilate” Iran if Tehran did not agree to a deal on the war.

Trump, whose war on Iran is nearing the seven-month mark, said US and Iranian officials would hold another round of talks in the “very near future”.

Jay Goldberg, a senior analyst at Seaport Research Partners in San Francisco, said signs of diplomatic progress between the US and Iran had refocused investor attention on the potential of AI to generate profits after years of multibillion-dollar investments.

“We have been searching for a clear consumer use case to justify the AI spend, and many see Muse as just that product,” Goldberg told Al Jazeera.

“Personally, I think Muse is just a step in the right direction; there will be better products – probably soon – but Muse is one of those things that are so useful they get investors excited about AI prospects again,” Goldberg said.

articles.title: Hiremath faces key shareholder vote
articles.summary: India Business News: MUMBAI: Sameer Hiremath faces a shareholder vote on Wednesday that will decide whether he becomes Hikal’s chairman for the first time. He is vice-chai.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Sameer Hiremath faces a shareholder vote on Wednesday that will decide whether he becomes Hikal’s chairman for the first time. He is vice-chairman and MD of the company, and a nephew of Baba Kalyani, chairman and MD of Bharat Forge.The vote follows the planned exit of his father, Jai Hiremath, 78, who steps down as chairman next month. It comes amid a bitter feud between the Hiremath and Kalyani branches of the family over assets worth more than Rs 1 lakh crore, with Supreme Court referring the dispute to mediation in July.Sameer’s appointment as CMD requires a simple majority under an ordinary resolution. The Hiremaths hold about 35% of Hikal, the Kalyani camp 34%. If Sameer, 52, cannot secure his uncle’s backing, the outcome will hinge on public shareholders, who own 31%. ICICI Prudential Fund and Tata Mutual Fund together hold about 6%.Proxy advisers are split, with IiAS and SES backing the appointment and InGovern against it. IiAS cited leadership continuity and Sameer’s three-decade association with Hikal; SES said it saw no major governance concerns. InGovern cited governance and board-independence concerns.IiAS noted that with Jai Hiremath’s exit, Sameer would become the sole executive representative of the Hiremath faction at a time when the wider Kalyani-Hiremath dispute, which also touches Hikal’s shareholding control, remains under mediation.Sugandha Hiremath, 74, Sameer’s mother and Baba’s sister, remains on Hikal’s board in a non-executive capacity. Sameer joined Hikal in Aug 1996 and has served on the board since May 1999. He holds 0.47% of Hikal directly and through Sameer Trust.InGovern acknowledged Sameer’s qualifications, extensive experience and his uninterrupted board attendance, but argued that combining the chairman and MD roles weakens the separation between oversight and management. Hikal, it said, had proposed no counterbalance such as an independent chair.Remote electronic voting closed on Tuesday. Shareholders who did not vote electronically can do so at Wednesday’s AGM, with results expected Thursday.The Hiremaths had taken divergent positions on the Kalyanis’ board reappointments in Hikal. In Dec 2023, they voted against Baba’s reappointment, ending his 31-year tenure on the board in Jan 2024. In Sept 2025, they backed the reappointment of his son, Amit Kalyani, vice-chairman and joint MD of Bharat Forge.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Trump buys up to $50,000 of Musk’s SpaceX, sells some a week later
articles.summary: International Business News: US President Donald Trump has continued to bet on Elon Musk’s aerospace giant SpaceX, buying between $15,001 and $50,000 worth of the firm’s shares ba.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has continued to bet on Elon Musk’s aerospace giant SpaceX, buying between $15,001 and $50,000 worth of the firm’s shares back in July. The transactions were part of a busy month for Trump’s portfolio, which saw 1,156 purchases and sales disclosed in July.According to a public financial disclosure, Trump made the purchase on July 10 and sold some of the shares a week later, on July 17. The SpaceX trades add to Trump’s investment activity involving Elon Musk’s companies, as he also bought and sold Tesla shares during the period.The combined value of those transactions was between roughly $79 million and $270 million, according to an estimation by CNBC. Of the total amount, purchases totalled at least $43.6 million, while sales amounted to at least $35.6 million.Trump’s investments in Musk’s companiesTrump had already reported buying between $15,001 and $50,000 worth of SpaceX shares on June 23. SpaceX went public on June 12 in the largest US IPO on record, with the space, satellite and AI provider valued at $1.77 trillion.SpaceX is a major Pentagon contractor and NASA launch provider. It also owns Musk’s xAI, which has a Pentagon contract worth up to $200 million.Musk was Trump’s biggest financial backer in 2024 and later served as an adviser to his administration.Trump also traded Tesla shares several times. He bought between $100,001 and $250,000 of Tesla on June 15 and between $15,001 and $50,000 the following day. He then sold between $131,004 and $365,000 across four transactions before buying another $100,001 to $250,000 of the automaker’s shares on July 27.Microsoft, Amazon among major July tradesTrump’s July trading extended well beyond Musk’s companies, with Microsoft and Amazon among the biggest transactions.On July 20, he sold between $5 million and $25 million worth of shares in each company. Three days later, he bought between $100,001 and $250,000 of Microsoft and between $1,001 and $15,000 of Amazon.The same July 20 filing showed Trump selling between $1 million and $5 million of Oracle and buying between $500,001 and $1 million of Nvidia.He also sold between $250,001 and $500,000 of Northrop Grumman shares that day. The trade took place on the same day Trump signed an executive order tightening supply chain requirements for defence contractors and restricting waivers for certain critical materials sourced from China and other covered countries. The disclosure does not show when the trade took place or who made the investment decision.Stocks, ETFs and bondsThe July disclosure also shows Trump buying between $1 million and $5 million each of Intuit, Marvell Technology, Salesforce and Church & Dwight. He bought between $250,000 and $500,000 of Axon Enterprises, which works frequently with Immigration and Customs Enforcement.Trump also moved money across exchange-traded funds. On July 8, he bought between $1 million and $5 million each of the State Street SPDR Bloomberg International Treasury Bond ETF, Fidelity MSCI Communication Services Index ETF, Vanguard Short-Term Bond Index Fund ETF and Vanguard Dividend Appreciation Index Fund ETF.On the same day, he sold between $1 million and $5 million each of the iShares US Treasury Bond ETF, State Street Communication Services Select Sector SPDR ETF and iShares International Treasury Bond ETF.Ten-year yields climbed on July 8, led by soaring oil prices, after Trump said at the NATO summit in Turkey that he thought a ceasefire with Iran was over.The filing also showed several large purchases of municipal and other bonds, including between $1 million and $5 million each of two Miami-Dade County, Florida, aviation revenue bonds, a St Louis County, Missouri, school district bond and a Main Street Natural Gas bond.Trading activity remains highThe July disclosure follows another heavy month of trading in June, when Trump reported 1,051 transactions worth between $78.1 million and $263.1 million across stocks, bonds and ETFs.His 2025 annual financial disclosure showed more than 21,000 securities trades across eight accounts holding at least $858 million. That compared with 86 stock transactions disclosed during his first year in office in 2017.The White House has repeatedly said Trump’s portfolio is managed independently and that neither he nor his family has a role in investment decisions.“President Trump’s stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third-party financial institutions,” White House spokesman Davis Ingle said in response to CNBC’s questions about Trump’s latest disclosure.“Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence, or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold.”Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Builder delayed Rs 44.36 lakh flat possession by 18 months and charged Rs 30,000 debris fee; Telangana RERA orders him to pay homebuyer 10.7% interest compensation for delay
articles.summary: India Business News: You pay for a flat which the builder promises possession of on an agreed timeline. He delays possession beyond the grace period. What do you do in suc.
articles.body: You pay for a flat which the builder promises possession of on an agreed timeline. He delays possession beyond the grace period. What do you do in such a case?Telangana RERA has granted relief to a homebuyer in one such case, ordering the building to pay interest compensation. It found that the builder had delayed handing over the flat by 18 months and had also levied an additional Rs 30,000 as a debris charge.The Telangana RERA authority concluded that the builder had not fulfilled its obligations under the Agreement of Sale and Section 11(4)(a) of the RERA Act. It also rejected the builder's contention that the delay was caused by Covid-19.What the case is aboutA man decided to purchase a flat after seeing an advertisement and checking information available on the builder's website. The flat, which was priced at Rs 44.36 lakh, was allotted to him.An Agreement of Sale was signed. The builder assured the homebuyer that the flat would be ready for possession by December 26, 2024. There was also an extended grace period available up to August 2025.Relying on these commitments, the homebuyer paid Rs 40.32 lakh towards the purchase of the flat. This included amounts that were charged for amenities, parking, EV charging and other allied facilities.The promised possession timelines, however, were repeatedly changed by the builder. The homebuyer said he was not given sufficient clarity about when construction would actually be completed, when the promised amenities would be ready or when the Occupancy Certificate would be obtained.There was also the issue of an additional debris charge of Rs 30,000. The homebuyer said this charge had not been disclosed earlier and did not form part of the agreement.The builder, on the other hand, stated that the project had reached nearly 85% completion. It also said that following discussions with homebuyers, the debris charge had been rationalised to Rs 20,000 per flat.Before the Telangana RERA authority, the homebuyer said the delay had put him under continuing financial pressure. He was having to meet his home loan EMI while simultaneously paying rent. He therefore sought interest compensation from the authority under the provisions of the RERA Act.What the builder saidThe builder defended the delay by saying that it was making efforts to complete the project within the revised deadline of December 2026. It cited several difficulties that had affected the construction schedule, including a shortage of labour, Covid-19 and legal issues relating to encroachment.He relied on the force majeure clause and cited the Covid-19 pandemic as a reason for the delay in the project. The builder also told Telangana RERA authority about an FTL encroachment issue involving some blocks in the society,According to the builder, these issues had a wider impact on the project. They led to operational setbacks, labour dispersal, panic among customers and the withdrawal of institutional funding.The builder further told the authority that the Telangana High Court subsequently clarified that construction work could proceed in blocks other than Blocks 8 and 9. It also said that the HMDA later confirmed there was no substantial FTL violation, apart from a minor issue that had already been rectified.The builder extended the construction deadline to December 18, 2026. This meant that possession of the flat would be delayed by more than 18 months from the originally committed timeline.On August 25, 2026, the homebuyer secured relief from Telangana RERA. The authority directed the builder to pay interest compensation at the rate of 10.7% for the delay in handing over possession, according to an ET report.Why homebuyer won the caseAsha Kiran Sharma, Partner at King Stubb and Kasiva, told ET that the Telangana RERA authority rejected the builder's reliance on Covid-19 and its subsequent consequences as an explanation for the delay.Sharma said the authority's reasoning centred on the timing of the Agreement of Sale. The agreement had been executed in February 2023, considerably after the pandemic had subsided.Therefore, according to the authority's reasoning, the builder had entered into its commitment to deliver possession with knowledge of the circumstances in which the project was being executed.It made it clear that the possession date that has been specified in the Agreement of Sale has to be taken into account.The authority also raised objections to the developer's actions on issues beyond the delay in handing over possession.One such issue was the Rs 30,000 "debris charge" added to the homebuyer's account. Telangana RERA rejected this charge, noting that it was not provided for in the Agreement of Sale and was inconsistent with the developer's statutory obligations under the RERA Act.Additionally, the payment record clearly showed that the homebuyer had paid Rs 40.32 lakh towards the total flat cost of Rs 44.36 lakh. These payments had been made without any default. Even after fulfilling his payment obligations, however, he did not receive possession by the committed date of December 26, 2024. The flat remained undelivered even after the expiry of the grace period.The Telangana RERA authority held that these circumstances amounted to a breach of the builder's contractual and statutory obligations under Section 18 of the RERA Act.The Telangana RERA authority said: “The material on record clearly demonstrates a continued pattern of false assurances despite the Respondent’s (builder’s) knowledge of its inability to adhere to the committed timelines, while the project admittedly remains incomplete beyond the stipulated possession date.”The Telangana RERA authority clarified that the homebuyer can seek compensation for mental agony, financial loss and any assured compensation amounts promised by the builder by filing an application in Form 'N' before the Adjudicating Officer under Section 71 of the RERA Act.The authority also struck down the debris charge imposed by the builder. It found that the charge was not supported by the terms of the Agreement of Sale and was contrary to Sections 11(4)(a), 11(4)(d) and 14 of the RERA Act.Telangana RERA directed that the homebuyer is entitled to interest compensation at the rate of 10.7% per annum.The interest is to be calculated on the amounts already paid by the homebuyer and will apply from June 26, 2025 until the date on which lawful possession of the flat is actually handed over.The authority directed the builder to clear the interest arrears accumulated up to the date of the order within 60 days. If the builder does not make the payment, the interest accruing thereafter will have to be paid every month, on or before the 10th day of the following month, until the homebuyer receives possession of the flat.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Nationwide strike: Banks to remain shut from Monday for three days - what customers need to know
articles.summary: India Business News: Do you have a pending bank visit, payment or other transactions lined up for the month-end? You may want to get it done by Friday!Banking operations a.
articles.body: Do you have a pending bank visit, payment or other transactions lined up for the month-end? You may want to get it done by Friday!Banking operations across the country are set to face disruption as bank unions have planed a three-day nationwide strike from September 28 to 30. With the strike following a weekend holiday, customers could face an effective five-day disruption in banking services.The timing is also significant as September 30 marks the half-yearly closing of banks, when reconciliation, provisioning, and treasury and market operations take place.What should customers do now?With banking services likely to face disruption around the end of September, customers may want to plan their banking requirements in advance. Several public sector banks have already advised customers to use digital channels if the strike goes ahead.Here’s what customers could do to avoid disruption:Complete branch-dependent work beforehand: Customers with requirements that need a branch visit or intervention from bank staff may need to plan them before the proposed strike period.Use mobile banking: Customers can use Mobile Banking for their banking needs.Use ATMs: ATMs are among the digital channels advised by public sector banks.Use internet banking: Customers can use Internet Banking for their banking needs.Use BC points: BC Points or business correspondents are also among the channels advised by public sector banks.Use UPI: Customers can use UPI for their banking needs.Services available through digital channels can continue to be accessed through those channels if the strike materialises. The disruption could also affect businesses, government transactions and international banking operations, apart from causing inconvenience to the public.Why are banks planning a strike?The United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU), which claims to represent 90 per cent of the banking workforce, has said it will proceed with the strike unless there is a concrete and positive development on its main demand for five-day banking.“Responding to the appeal made by the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Indian Banks' Association (IBA), Bank managements to defer the strike, we informed them that if there is any concrete and positive development towards implementation of our demand for introduction of 5 days banking, UFBU will consider the same,” UFBU said in a statement after the meeting with the deputy chief labour commissioner.The statement came after a conciliation meeting on Tuesday remained inconclusive. The union said that in the absence of such a development, it would be constrained to go ahead with the proposed strike on September 28, 29 and 30.The meeting was held a day after the finance ministry appealed to bank employees to refrain from strikes and resolve their remaining demands through dialogue.UFBU's other demands include an update and improvement of pension, a uniform dearness allowance formula for all pensioners and an option for employees covered under the National Pension System (NPS) to move to the old pension scheme (OPS).Bank unions under the UFBU had also gone on a nationwide strike on September 11 over their demands.What has the government said?Representatives of the department of financial services (DFS) and the ministry of finance told the conciliation meeting that the government had been taking several initiatives for the welfare of bank employees. They said five-day banking was also under consideration, but the government would need to take into account the views of various other stakeholders before taking a decision.The representatives therefore asked the UFBU to defer the strike and continue the dialogue.The finance ministry had said that strikes disrupt banking services, inconvenience the public and affect the business of banks. It also said such disruptions ultimately harm the interests of bank employees and that no fruitful outcome is achieved through strikes.The government has assured that it remains committed to the welfare and well-being of bank employees and to addressing their genuine concerns through constructive engagement.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Precio de la luz por horas hoy, miércoles 23 de septiembre: cuándo es más barata y más cara en el día
articles.standfirst: El precio de la luz sube moderadamente este miércoles
articles.summary: El precio de la luz sube moderadamente este miércoles
articles.body: El precio medio de la electricidad para hoy, 158,88 €/MWh, se mantiene por encima del día anterior, cuando era 156,02 €/MWh, lo que supone una diferencia de 2,86 €. Este miércoles, los consumidores deben estar atentos a las horas más caras y más baratas del día, ya que pueden influir en su factura eléctrica. Los precios de la luz alcanzan su máximo entre las 20:00 y las 22:00, con un bloque continuo altamente costoso. Durante este periodo, la luz se sitúa en valores que superan los 263 €/MWh, alcanzando un peak de 263.89 €/MWh a las 20:00 - 21:00 y manteniéndose en cifras elevadas como 239.46 €/MWh a las 21:00 - 22:00. Además, se observa otro tramo significativo entre las 19:00 - 20:00 y las 22:00 - 23:00, donde los precios se mantienen por encima de los 220 €/MWh. Este patrón de precios refleja una clara concentración de costos elevados en un bloque horario que debería ser considerado por los consumidores. Las oportunidades de ahorro en el costo de la luz se concentran principalmente durante la madrugada y las primeras horas del día. Los tramos más destacados son entre las 12:00 - 13:00 con un precio de 35.0 €/MWh y 13:00 - 14:00 donde alcanza el mínimo de 15.03 €/MWh. Estos precios bajos se mantienen hasta las 14:00 - 15:00 (25.05 €/MWh) y aumentan paulatinamente a partir de entonces. La ventana de ahorro se extiende por más de dos horas, que representa una clara oportunidad para optimizar el consumo eléctrico. El análisis de las franjas horarias de este miércoles revela una notable diferencia de precios entre las horas más caras y las más baratas, alcanzando hasta 248,86 €/MWh entre el precio máximo y el mínimo del día. Esta variabilidad resalta la importancia de seleccionar cuidadosamente el momento para consumir energía, ya que los consumidores pueden beneficiarse significativamente de la planificación de su consumo eléctrico.
